items.t: Is Equinix (EQIX) Fully Valued As SG6 Opens And Green Notes Fund Growth?
sum: Equinix (EQIX) is back in focus after opening its AI ready SG6 data center in Singapore and issuing €2.5b in green senior notes, a paired move that directly shapes future capacity and funding.

Recent trading has reflected that story. Equinix’s share price is up 37.91% year to date and the 1 year total shareholder return is 37.01%, even though the 90 day share price return declined 4.38%. This points to strong longer term momentum with some near term cooling as investors digest the SG6 launch, green financing and new AI partnerships.
Scan how Equinix’s AI ready buildout compares with other digital infrastructure players by reviewing our curated list of 53 AI infrastructure stocks.
Equinix now has fresh AI-ready capacity, a €2.5b green funding pool, and a US$106.2b market value on the line. Is that powerful setup already fully reflected in the price, or not yet?

Equinix last closed at $1,053.79, while the leading community valuation in the narrative pegs fair value closer to $938.23. The discussion therefore starts with a gap that leans rich on the current share price according to LunaRodas, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the narrative.

The atNorth transaction, closed this quarter, adds 800 megawatts of active development and another gigawatt of future optionality, recognized through the equity method rather than consolidation. Fox-Martin frames capacity expansion as ahead of plan and notes the company has exceeded its original retail capacity target for the year by nearly 40%.
Still, pressure on data center financing and power availability could challenge Equinix’s capacity plans and turn today’s valuation gap into a much tighter spread.

Equinix stock: Company completes EUR 2.5 billion green bond issue
sum: Equinix объявила во вторник, 10 ноября, что ее финансовая дочерняя компания выпустила зеленые старшие облигации на сумму 2,5 миллиарда евро четырьмя траншами. Размещение завершилось 9 ноября и является крупнейшим выпуском зеленых старших облигаций компании на сегодняшний день, согласно репродукции Trivano объявления Equinix.

По облигациям эффективная совокупная процентная ставка составляет 4,82 процента годовых на смешанной основе с учетом предполагаемого воздействия хеджирования процентных ставок. Equinix гарантирует облигации, и ожидается, что чистые поступления пойдут на финансирование или рефинансирование соответствующих критериям проектов в соответствии с обновленной структурой зеленого финансирования.

Подходящие категории включают зеленые здания, возобновляемую и чистую энергию, энергоэффективность, устойчивое управление водными ресурсами и устойчивость водосборов. Equinix заявила, что новый выпуск увеличит совокупный объем зеленых облигаций выше 12 миллиардов долларов США во всем мире.

Финансовый директор Оливье Леонетти заявил, что высокий спрос на предложение отражает уверенность инвесторов в долгосрочной стратегии роста Equinix. Для акционеров финансирование расширяет возможности финансирования, добавляя при этом старшие обязательства, стоимость и распределение которых будут оставаться актуальными для будущих доходов.

В отчете о распределении и воздействии зеленых облигаций за 2026 год говорится, что все доходы от непогашенных ранее выпусков зеленых облигаций Equinix были распределены по состоянию на июнь 2026 года. Следующий вопрос инвесторов заключается в том, поддерживают ли финансируемые проекты расширение мощностей и регулярные доходы без ослабления дисциплины капитала.
Акции Equinix торговались на уровне 944,00 евро на бирже Lang & Schwarz в 16:35 по центральноевропейскому времени в пятницу, 13 ноября 2026 года.

Equinix stock tracks AI capacity expansion with SG6 opening
sum: Equinix opened SG6 in Singapore on November 6, adding capacity for artificial intelligence, high-performance computing and data-intensive workloads. The company said in its press release that the facility is its sixth International Business Exchange data center in the city-state.

Equinix stock traded at 969.20 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 5:00 p.m. CET on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, up 7.38 percent from 902.60 euros in our November 5 report. The comparison reflects the move since that report and is separate from any daily Xetra comparison.

The first phase represents an initial investment of approximately 290 million US dollars and provides 8 MW across approximately 1,550 cabinets. Full build-out is planned to reach up to 20 MW of IT capacity, giving Equinix additional infrastructure in one of Asia-Pacific's key connectivity markets.

SG6 is designed for high-density AI deployments through proprietary cooling systems and liquid-cooling capabilities for power-intensive GPU infrastructure. Equinix also cited rooftop and facade solar photovoltaic systems, rainwater harvesting and lower-embodied-carbon construction materials. The site is designed for a power usage effectiveness ratio of 1.20 and is targeting Green Mark Platinum certification.

Equinix plans to open a Co-Innovation Facility at SG6 with the National University of Singapore in 2027. The facility is intended to focus on liquid cooling, cognitive digital twins and battery energy storage systems, linking the Singapore expansion with research on data center sustainability and energy efficiency.

For investors, SG6 adds physical capacity to Equinix's exposure to cloud connectivity and AI infrastructure demand. The company has not disclosed SG6-specific customer revenue or utilization figures, so the near-term financial contribution cannot be measured from the opening announcement alone.

David Sacks Warns the AI Data Center Pipeline Could Dry Up. Here’s What’s at Stake
sum: A permitting fight could stall the buildings that every AI chip, cable, and cooling system needs. While chip stocks sank in a single month, one corner of the market barely flinched. Which suppliers are exposed, and who collects rent either…
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

David Sacks thinks the AI data center boom could run out of road within about two years. On the All-In podcast episode released November 7, which covered the midterm elections, the AI selloff, and what the hosts called a data center freeze, David Sacks said: “Nobody can make a $50 billion investment in conditions of uncertainty. I think by 2028 the pipeline will be closed or significantly reduced.”

His argument rests on permitting. Sacks said the biggest danger is breaking ground and then, halfway through, getting “enjoined” or stopped by a worker strike or a community group. According to Sacks, governors in the largest data center states are “basically indicating that they favor a moratorium” until certain conditions are met.

A data center needs land, power, and a finished building before a single chip goes in. Broadcom’s chief executive made the same point on the company’s September call: “Before you get the chips out there, you have to get the data center shell in place and ready for production.” If the buildings stall, chip, networking, and cooling orders slow down after them.
That dependency matters because each company in the chain is posting growth that assumes the expansion keeps going:

- The company, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA | NVDA Price Prediction), reported Data Center revenue of $89.02B, up 117%, guided next quarter to $108.0B +/- 2%, and disclosed supply obligations of $279.00B in its latest earnings release filed with the SEC.

Equinix stock: Record bookings support a third 2026 outlook raise
sum: Equinix strengthened its growth case after reporting record third-quarter bookings and raising its 2026 outlook for the third consecutive quarter. The update followed results for the period ended September 30, 2026, released on October 28 in the company's third-quarter results release.

Annualized gross bookings reached 533 million US dollars, an increase of 35 percent from a year earlier. Third-quarter revenue rose 11 percent to 2.571 billion US dollars on an as-reported basis, while normalized and constant-currency growth was 12 percent.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 15 percent to 1.321 billion US dollars. Adjusted funds from operations rose 20 percent to 1.156 billion US dollars, while AFFO per diluted share reached 11.64 US dollars on a reported basis. Equinix said a non-recurring fee related to its atNorth investment supported that comparison.

Chief Executive Adaire Fox-Martin said Equinix was accelerating capacity delivery to meet broad-based demand. The company introduced Fabric One for distributed cloud, network and AI environments and announced Equinix Inference Exchange with NVIDIA and Together AI.

Nearly 40 percent more cabinets are planned for delivery in 2026 than initially expected. For the full year, Equinix expects revenue of 10.325 billion to 10.365 billion US dollars, adjusted EBITDA of 5.290 billion to 5.330 billion US dollars and AFFO of 4.340 billion to 4.380 billion US dollars. Fourth-quarter revenue is forecast at 2.684 billion to 2.724 billion US dollars, with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 49 to 50 percent.

Equinix stock: Record bookings support third outlook raise
sum: Equinix reported record demand and raised its full-year outlook again after the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. In its October 28 results release, the data center operator reported annualized gross bookings of 533 million US dollars, up 35 percent from a year earlier.

Third-quarter revenue rose 11 percent year over year on an as-reported basis to 2.571 billion US dollars. On a normalized and constant-currency basis, revenue increased 12 percent. Monthly recurring revenue grew at a double-digit rate for the fourth consecutive quarter, while interconnection revenue advanced 10 percent.

Adjusted EBITDA reached 1.321 billion US dollars, up 15 percent as reported and 14 percent on a normalized and constant-currency basis. Adjusted funds from operations rose 20 percent as reported to 1.156 billion US dollars. AFFO per diluted share increased 18 percent as reported to 11.64 US dollars, or 12 percent on a normalized basis excluding the benefit of a fee related to the atNorth joint venture.

Net income attributable to common stockholders rose 31 percent to 489 million US dollars, and diluted earnings per share increased 29 percent to 4.93 US dollars. The company said the net income comparison benefited partly from a non-recurring fee connected with its atNorth investment, making the normalized AFFO figures more relevant for assessing recurring operating momentum.

Chief Executive Adaire Fox-Martin said the company was accelerating capacity to meet broad-based demand. Equinix also introduced Fabric One, a connectivity service for distributed cloud, network and AI environments, and announced Equinix Inference Exchange with NVIDIA and Together AI. The company said nearly 40 percent more cabinets were planned for delivery in 2026 than initially expected.

For the fourth quarter, Equinix expects revenue of 2.684 billion to 2.724 billion US dollars and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 49 to 50 percent. For the full year, revenue guidance now stands at 10.325 billion to 10.365 billion US dollars, adjusted EBITDA at 5.290 billion to 5.330 billion US dollars and AFFO at 4.340 billion to 4.380 billion US dollars. The company expects full-year revenue growth of about 12 percent and AFFO per share growth of 11 to 12 percent on a normalized and constant-currency basis.

Equinix stock: Q3 growth drives a third 2026 guidance raise
sum: Equinix reported stronger third-quarter operations on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, and raised its full-year outlook for the third consecutive quarter. The company said demand remained broad across connectivity, data centers and artificial-intelligence workloads.

According to the Equinix investor release, third-quarter revenue increased 11 percent year over year to 2.571 billion US dollars. Normalized revenue growth at constant currency was 12 percent, while adjusted EBITDA rose 15 percent to 1.321 billion US dollars and the margin reached 51 percent.

Annualized gross bookings reached a record 533 million US dollars, up 35 percent from the prior year. Equinix added 6,900 net interconnections, while interconnection revenue rose 10 percent and Fabric revenue increased 24 percent.

Net income attributable to common stockholders rose 31 percent to 489 million US dollars, or 4.93 US dollars per diluted share. The result included a non-recurring fee related to the atNorth joint venture. Diluted AFFO per share increased 18 percent as reported and 12 percent on a normalized, constant-currency basis excluding that fee.

Equinix now expects 2026 revenue of 10.325 billion to 10.365 billion US dollars, compared with the previous range of 10.205 billion to 10.285 billion US dollars. Adjusted EBITDA guidance moved to 5.290 billion to 5.330 billion US dollars, while AFFO per share is expected at 43.71 to 44.11 US dollars.

For the fourth quarter, management expects revenue of 2.684 billion to 2.724 billion US dollars and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 49 to 50 percent. Total capital expenditures for 2026, excluding real-estate acquisitions and xScale, remain planned at 5 billion to 6 billion US dollars. Nearly 40 percent more cabinets than initially anticipated are scheduled for delivery in 2026, raising execution and funding requirements alongside the growth opportunity.

Why Did Equinix (NASDAQ:EQIX) Shares Dip Despite a Raised Range?
sum: - Equinix (NASDAQ:EQIX) Real Estate Equinix Inc (NASDAQ:EQIX) 993.69 USD -20.010 1.974% Last Updated at: 2026-11-02T21:00:00Z raised its full-year range and multi-year growth ambitions at its latest-quarter report.
- Equinix filed details on xScale ventures, capacity spending and note issuance in its quarterly report.
- Power availability and customer demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure remain central to the Equinix story.

The most recent reference points are the latest-quarter results delivered at the end of July and the quarterly report filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, which together described rising revenue, a lifted full-year range and a sharply improved multi-year growth ambition, even though the quarter-ahead revenue range disappointed some market participants. Demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure, power availability and heavy capital spending are the main storylines surrounding the name.

At the end of July, Equinix reported latest-quarter revenue that came in above what the market had anticipated, and it raised its full-year revenue range along with its range for adjusted funds from operations per share. News reports noted that shares moved lower on the day because the revenue range given for the following quarter had a midpoint a little under expectations. That reaction illustrates how a stock can fall even on a beat and a raise.

Alongside the quarterly numbers, management raised its multi-year expectations. According to press coverage, the company now expects annual revenue growth in a higher band than before, running through the end of the decade, and a similarly upgraded range for growth in adjusted funds from operations per share. Such a revision signals management's belief that the demand cycle for digital infrastructure has strengthened.

sum: Equinix Inc. received an Outperformer rating and a USD 1,200.00 price target from CIBC on October 21, 2026, giving investors a fresh benchmark before the data center operator reports third-quarter results. According to Markets Insider, analyst Stephanie Price initiated coverage with the rating and target. Equinix stock was trading at EUR 889.90 at Lang & Schwarz on October 27, 2026 at 4:41 p.m. CEST.

Equinix reported USD 2.63 billion in revenue for the second quarter of fiscal 2026, ended June 30, 2026. Revenue increased 16.40 percent from the prior-year quarter, while net income attributable to common stockholders rose 30.20 percent to USD 479.0 million.

Adjusted funds from operations reached USD 1.17 billion in the second quarter, an increase of 20.20 percent year over year. Recurring revenue was USD 2.38 billion, up 10.90 percent, although one-time fees from Americas xScale joint ventures also lifted the quarter's figures, according to Ticker Scout.

The CIBC target stood 20.82 percent above the Nasdaq price of USD 993.27 at 11:48 a.m. ET on October 27, 2026. The same quote showed a market capitalization of USD 98.0 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 63.94 and a 52-week range of USD 720.62 to USD 1,128.68.

Equinix's next reporting date is October 28, 2026, when the company is scheduled to publish third-quarter results. MarketScreener lists the third-quarter earnings release on that date, placing the next operating update immediately after the latest analyst action.

The second-quarter revenue increase provides the operating benchmark for the upcoming release. Investors will be able to compare the next quarter's revenue and adjusted funds from operations with the prior figures of USD 2.63 billion and USD 1.17 billion, respectively.

sum: Equinix, Inc. EQIX is scheduled to report third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 28, after market close. The company's quarterly results are likely to display a year-over-year rise in revenues and adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) per share.

In the previous quarter, this Redwood City, CA-based data center real estate investment trust (REIT) reported an AFFO of $10.78 per share, outpacing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $11.25. The results reflected higher recurring revenues on stronger underlying demand and robust bookings. Non-recurring revenues more than doubled, driven primarily by xScale leasing fees.

Over the preceding four quarters, EQIX's AFFO per share surpassed the consensus estimate on two occasions and missed in the remaining quarters, with the average beat being 2.05%. This is depicted in the graph below:

In the third quarter of 2026, Equinix is likely to have benefited from the solid demand for interconnected data center infrastructure. Enterprises' and service providers' continued efforts to integrate artificial intelligence into their strategies and offerings and advance their digital transformation agendas are likely to keep demand up in the upcoming years.

Moreover, the demand for Equinix's interconnected ecosystem is likely to have remained strong, driven by accelerating enterprise cloud adoption and increasing demand from cloud and internet customers for highly interconnected data center space.

The company's recurring revenue model, which comprises colocation, related interconnection and managed infrastructure services, is expected to have supported stable cash flows in the to-be-reported quarter, boosting the data center REIT's top line.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for colocation revenues is pegged at $1.81 billion, suggesting growth from $1.64 billion in the prior-year period. The consensus mark for interconnection revenues is pinned at $469.6 million, indicating growth from $422 million in the prior-year period.

sum: CIBC began coverage of Equinix with an Outperform rating and a USD 1,200.00 price target on October 21, 2026, according to MarketScreener. The target was 20.60 percent above Equinix's Nasdaq close of USD 995.00 on October 21, 2026. Equinix stock was trading at EUR 840.40 at Lang & Schwarz on October 22, 2026 at 4:39 p.m. CEST.

The CIBC initiation adds a fresh analyst view to a stock covered by 35 analysts, whose average target was USD 1,231.88 on the MarketScreener overview dated October 21, 2026. The average target stood 23.81 percent above the listed Nasdaq close of USD 995.00, while the CIBC target was lower than that average.

Equinix operates specialized real estate investment trusts focused on data centers and interconnection. Its business profile lists 280 data centers at the end of 2025, with 44.60 percent of net sales from the Americas, 34.00 percent from Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and 21.40 percent from Asia-Pacific, according to MarketScreener.

Equinix has scheduled its third-quarter results conference call for October 28, 2026, at 5:30 p.m. ET. The official investor-relations calendar confirms the date and call time, while the company release says the discussion will cover the period ended September 30, 2026, according to Equinix and Equinix newsroom. The scheduled date gives investors a defined event for testing the growth assumptions behind the USD 1,200.00 target.

The Nasdaq close of USD 995.00 on October 21, 2026 provides the latest completed home-market reference in the available company quote. The German euro quotation stood at EUR 840.40 at Lang & Schwarz on October 22, 2026 at 4:39 p.m. CEST, so the two figures should be read as separate venue prices rather than combined into one percentage.

For investors, the immediate test is the October 28 report rather than another target revision. CIBC's USD 1,200.00 target and the USD 1,231.88 analyst average both sit above the October 21 Nasdaq close, while the upcoming report will provide the next operating checkpoint.

sum: Equinix Inc. stock (ISIN US29444U7033) is back in the analyst spotlight after Rothschild Redburn initiated coverage with a buy rating and a price target of USD 1,261.00, implying about 23 percent upside from recent levels as reported on September 21, 2026.Investing.com For investors, the combination of premium valuation and continued growth in digital infrastructure is now the central question.

According to Investing.com on September 21, 2026, Rothschild Redburn launched coverage of Equinix Inc. with a buy recommendation and set a price target of USD 1,261.00 per share, describing the stock as commanding a premium valuation in the specialized REITs segment with a price-to-earnings ratio around 66.

The firm’s target suggests around 23 percent upside versus the prevailing market price at the time of the initiation, indicating that the analyst team expects Equinix to continue monetizing demand for data center and interconnection services despite regulatory and permitting headwinds in some jurisdictions.Investing.com For shareholders, the new coverage adds another supportive voice to a sector where visibility on long-term demand is a key driver of valuation.

In the wider data center real estate investment trust peer group, Mizuho continues to rate both Equinix and Digital Realty at Outperform, pointing to potential gains for the segment even as some state-level authorities in the United States express reservations about the expansion of large-scale data centers due to power and land-use concerns.Investing.com Korea This mix of supportive analyst views and policy debate forms an important backdrop for Equinix Inc. stock.

The sector framing matters because Equinix’s valuation premium, as reflected in the roughly 66 times earnings multiple cited by Rothschild Redburn,Investing.com relies on continued confidence that data center demand, interconnection needs and enterprise cloud migration will sustain double-digit growth in key metrics for years. A key risk is that environmental and grid constraints could slow down capacity additions and pressurize returns, which is why investors watch permitting and regulatory developments alongside earnings.

CoreWeave Shares Sink After Bernstein Warns Of Slower AI Training
sum: CoreWeave CRWV shares fell 6% Monday as investors weighed the potential impact of slower artificial intelligence model training on data-center demand, according to a Monday investor note from Bernstein.
Analyst Maidson Rezaei said facilities in rural and Tier 3 markets could face greater pressure because many were developed around training workloads that are less sensitive to network latency.

Bernstein estimates about 70% of a 488-gigawatt U.S. data-center development pipeline is located in rural or Tier 3 areas. CoreWeave has about 25% of its active U.S. power and roughly 74% of contracted power in Tier 3 and Tier 4 markets.

The firm said CoreWeave's existing backlog is largely supported by take-or-pay agreements, which may limit near-term risk. However, demand for contracted capacity that has not yet been sold could weaken if training activity slows.

Equinix EQIX, Digital Realty Trust DLR and Csquare CSQR may be less exposed because most of their capacity is located in metropolitan markets. Bernstein rates CoreWeave Underperform with a $74 target, while assigning Outperform ratings to the other three.

sum: Equinix (EQIX) came out with quarterly funds from operations (FFO) of $11.78 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $11.25 per share. This compares to FFO of $9.91 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an FFO surprise of +4.71%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this data center operator would post FFO of $10.89 per share when it actually produced FFO of $10.79, delivering a surprise of -0.92%.
Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus FFO estimates two times.

Equinix, which belongs to the Zacks REIT and Equity Trust - Retail industry, posted revenues of $2.63 billion for the quarter ended June 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.34%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $2.26 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates just once over the last four quarters.
The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future FFO expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.
Equinix shares have added about 35.1% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 8.5%.
While Equinix has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

Equinix Stock Has A Message For Management
sum: The company raised its outlook on booming AI demand, but the stock is telling a different story by standing still.

Back on Apr 29, 2026, Equinix (EQIX) management did what you want to see management do: they took a public victory lap. Citing a surge in AI-driven demand, the company raised its full-year revenue target to $10.19 Bil. The market’s reaction since? A shrug. The stock has returned a perfectly flat +0.05%, leaving investors with a simple, nagging question: If the AI story is this good, what’s the holdup?

Management certainly laid out a compelling case. Q1, they said, was the “largest quarter of total sales activity in our history,” with that activity up more than 35% year-over-year. The engine for this growth is clear: executives noted that “approximately 60% of our largest deals in Q1 were AI-related.” The work involves building the interconnected plumbing for the AI revolution, a more fundamental task than simply filling racks. The company’s high-margin interconnection services are booming, with bookings for its Fabric platform soaring 70% year-over-year. This is the story that powered the guidance raise and created a record backlog. Yet, the stock price suggests the market heard the story but is waiting for the punchline.

The market seems to be looking past the booming sales and focusing on the price tag. To meet this demand, Equinix is spending heavily. The company now expects total capital expenditures to hit the top end of its prior range at $4.1 billion for the year. That’s a massive outlay, and it brings the central tension for the stock into sharp focus. Investors have long prized Equinix for its high returns on capital. The fear, bubbling under the surface, is whether these new, power-hungry AI workloads require so much more expensive infrastructure that they will inevitably dilute the very profitability that made the stock a winner.

For their part, executives insist the discipline that got them here isn’t going anywhere. They are still underwriting new projects to deliver returns in the “mid-20s percent,” even with the higher-density requirements of AI. But the market is in a “show-me” state. It has seen the forecast and heard the promises.

Equinix Hires Former Juniper Channel Chief Gordon Mackintosh To Lead Global Partner Sales
sum: ‘Gordon knows both the OEM and partner side of the business and has what it takes to bring all the pieces of the puzzle together for Equinix,’ says Advizex CEO C.R. Howdyshell.

Gordon Mackintosh, who until recently was heading up the combined HPE-Juniper partner networking business, has been tapped by $9.2 billion data center and colocation behemoth Equinix to lead global partner sales.

“This week, I take on a new challenge and have joined Equinix as SVP of Partner Sales and Programs,” said Mackintosh (pictured) in a LinkedIn post that comes nearly one month after HPE said he was leaving to pursue another opportunity. “Equinix has built something truly special, and I’m excited to build on that strong foundation—evolving the partner motion, unlocking incremental value, and helping turn it into an even more powerful growth engine for the company. Really looking forward to help shape what’s ahead!!!”

C.R. Howdyshell, CEO of Independence, Ohio-based Advizex, No. 129 on the 2025 CRN Solution Provider 500, an Equinix partner, said bringing Mackintosh on board to drive channel growth is a “huge” coup for the colocation provider.

“Gordon knows both the OEM and partner side of the business and has what it takes to bring all the pieces of the puzzle together for Equinix,” said Howdyshell. “For partners like us there is a significant opportunity to sell our managed services working hand in hand with Equinix, which is very flexible and has a good channel program.”

Howdyshell said he is looking forward to working with Mackintosh to expand Advizex’s business with the company. “We see significant opportunities to drive customer colocation adoption with Equinix, building on the success we have already had,” he said.
Howdyshell said “most customers do not want to be in the data center business” and are looking for more cost-effective ways to run workloads with a colocation provider like Equinix.
